summary: ACCEPT. Fixes the ~60 percent scanner-history flake that was corrupting mutation evidence across today's whole batch - it nearly manufactured a false 'mutant dies' inside a review. ⭐ The test is a genuine REPRODUCTION, not a retry: it monkeypatches utcnow to a FIXED value so every append observes the identical wall clock, which is the real failure condition on a coarse-resolution clock, and the author reports that a first timestamp-only attempt still reproduced the failure before landing on this approach. The assertion mirrors PRODUCTION's ordering including its tie-break - retention orders by desc(created_at), desc(id) at strategy_engine_app.py:9489 and the test now orders by (created_at, id) - so it is not inventing an order that only the test uses. Mechanism: on insert, read the prior max created_at FOR THAT snapshot_type and force created_at = max(now, prior + 1 microsecond); a backward clock step also stays monotonic, and drift is 1us per insert so it is negligible. ⛔ BLAST RADIUS to record: the change is in the SHARED _append_dashboard_snapshot, so it applies to EVERY snapshot type, not just scanner_cycle_history. That is benign and probably beneficial for the #823 D2 FanoutOutcomeJournal, whose keyset cursor at fanout_outcome_consumer.py:291-304 orders by (created_at, id) and whose own docstring names this exact hazard - 'terminal can therefore otherwise share created_at and replay in random UUID order'. ⚠ Note there are now TWO independent monotonic-timestamp mechanisms writing this one table: _next_recorded_at() in the fanout consumer and this DB-read approach. They do not collide because the probe filters by snapshot_type, but a future reader will ask which is authoritative. ⛔ MEASURED PERFORMANCE, required follow-up: dashboard_snapshots has indexes on id and snapshot_type ONLY, so the pre-insert probe does a top-N heapsort - EXPLAIN ANALYZE on production shows 6.891ms and 837 shared buffer hits for a single row, on a 237MB / 5068-row table, and the cost scales with table size. Acceptable today because the path is dashboard state rather than order flow, but it runs on EVERY snapshot insert. Add index (snapshot_type, created_at DESC, id DESC) to make it O(1).
